page: Amazon Web Services c6in.12xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (Ice Lake 8375C). The instance provides 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores running at a sustained all-core frequency of up to 3.5 GHz. Memory is configured at 96.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This configuration includes 54 MB of shared L3 cache alongside instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs and features no local instance storage, relying entirely on network-attached Amazon Elastic Block Store.

A key hardware attribute of the c6in generation is its elevated networking capability, delivering a 75 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the upper quartile for vector and cryptographic throughput, demonstrated by top-tier results in PassMark CPU encryption tests, Geekbench ray tracing, and Geekbench image processing. Instruction processing for machine learning shows competitive CPU inference on smaller models, supported by AVX-512 VNNI hardware acceleration. General integer, multi-threaded decompression, and standard memory bandwidth benchmarks reflect expected mid-tier performance typical of 48-vCPU Ice Lake deployments.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the c6in.12xlarge targets workloads demanding dense compute paired with high throughput data transfers. Because the instance provisions no bundled local storage, storage-heavy architectures incur external EBS costs. However, the high baseline network capacity reduces network interface bottlenecks for distributed applications. Workload fit includes high-performance computing (HPC), network virtual appliances, distributed analytics, static web serving nodes, Clang software build farms, and batch encryption tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c6in.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors on the AWS Nitro architecture. It features 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores operating at 3.5 GHz, 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include discrete GPUs or local disk storage, depending completely on network-attached storage. Architectural extensions include AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and hardware-accelerated cryptography. Benchmark assessments demonstrate top-quartile performance in cryptographic encryption, ray tracing, image processing, and lightweight model prompt evaluation, while general multi-core compute tests align with the median for its core count. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio paired with high network capability makes this instance technically suited for network-intensive batch processing, clustered computational tasks, continuous integration software compilation, distributed web serving, and mid-scale analytics pipelines requiring heavy inter-node data exchange.
